description:
LANDED dd07432db on wt/kdt-close (PR #110, draft), 2026-09-03. Research with
prototype, cold review (approve-with-fixes, ten fixes folded), rebased onto
fz-kdt.194.

THE RULE: an activation's published return may depend only on what its key
names. A slot POSITION is on the key when a dispatch question reaches it
(fz-kdt.183) OR when the activation's published return is built from it and
the recursion does not supply it (this ticket). FactKey::InputDemand gains a
third axis, `returned`, solved by the SAME Kleene iteration over the SAME
forwarding cone -- no new fact, no new wait (DeriveInputDemand evaluations
unchanged at 256/149/190). A returned `Whole` keeps the addressed convergence
class rather than the type verbatim, so fz-kdt.200's no-collapse hole does not
widen (grow/2 2 keys base and head).

THE DEFECT: a returned tuple FIELD at a recursive key was freight. `{:done,
acc}` is masked TupleFields({0: Whole}) -- the key names the TAG only -- while
the activation's return IS that field, so two users of one walker shared one
key and one JOINED return. Measured red at base on all three doors:
returned_tuple_field_keys_its_users_apart.fz reports error[spec/violation]
([binary] | [int]) on a legitimate program, and prints 1 / [9] here.

WIDER THAN THE TICKET SAID, and this corrects a LANDED law: `loop(0, junk),
do: junk` -- fz-kdt.183's own first keying law, blessed as "freight must key
ONE activation" -- has the identical defect at base (spec/violation on all
three doors; prints 1 / [1, 2] here). That law is a COST pin, not a
correctness one. The distinction is real, not a retraction: carry/2, the same
shape but which does NOT return the slot, correctly stays at one key. The
ONE_ACTIVATION_KEYING_LAWS gate message, which still said "fz-kdt.183 keys a
slot on DEMAND, not on structure", now names both axes.

THE SUBTRACTION IS A LEAST FIXPOINT, and that is load-bearing. "Minus the
positions the recursion supplies" is what keeps freight collapsed, but the
eager form (held_slot == slot && held_path == path) poisons a pure
PERMUTATION: `go(0, a, _b), do: a` / `go(n, a, b), do: go(n - 1, b, a)`
supplies nothing, yet both slots read as rebuilt, so base AND the eager
prototype both emit spec/violation from one key publishing the join. The
correct rule -- a position is supplied only if its value is held nowhere, or
only at positions themselves supplied -- cures it. The builder built the
eager variant to prove the difference: it keys go/3 ONCE and leaves swap.fz
broken; the fixpoint keys it twice, and against the eager prototype the
fixpoint is FREE (0 canon movers, identical executables). Without the
subtraction entirely: split3/5 1 -> 8, split4/6 1 -> 16, tag/3 1 -> 3,
quicksort 17 -> 20, and it buys nothing.

MEASURED (604 fixtures / 475 dumps, against ca23b676f; method stated:
grep -c '^  executable ' over the dumps, stdout+stderr normalised for thread
id, backtrace addresses and the embedded build path per fz-kdt.211): interp 0
movers, run 0 movers; canon 33 movers of which 13 change key text only;
executables 5469 -> 5536 (+67); arms fall sharply (00277 68 -> 26,
enum_map_family 103 -> 61, fz_f98_range_map_converges 30 -> 10). On the cold
review's 597-list/469-dump comparand this reproduces the review to the digit
(5282 -> 5357, 29 movers). FIFO/LIFO: base 2 movers / 5469 both ways, head the
SAME 2 movers / 5536 both ways, 0 run movers. Freight rows carry/2, tag/3,
split3/5, split4/6, fwd/2 all hold at ONE activation; quicksort frontier
unmoved at 17; the rung gate reads 23, none on freight. lib 1709/0/5; matrix
509/0/9 (+3 = the new fixture's three doors, verified by --list).

THE COST, PUBLISHED NOT HIDDEN: pull.product.settled 9815 -> 12406 (+26%) on
enum_take_drop_split, pinned beside the span count because the span census
understates it. The wall-clock "faster" claim the research made is WITHDRAWN
(best-of-5 463 -> 452 ms is noise). Of the added executables 36 buy a distinct
return and 91 do not (83 on the review's comparand), dominated by
List.reduce_cont/3 (21), reduce_while_cont/3 (18), Range.reduce_while_cont/6
(9) and reduce_while_step/3 (6) -- the build/2 gate records this as a PIN, not
a law, and names fz-kdt.213 as its removal ticket.

RESIDUES, EACH OWNED: fz-kdt.213 (the subtraction is self-only, so a mutual
cycle it cannot see mints the 91 unbought executables); fz-kdt.214 (the
returned axis reuses forwarded_inputs, which ignores a DirectCall dest and
sees neither reconstructed nor projected arguments -- hops.fz, proto_cb.fz,
deliver2.fz); fz-kdt.182 (union(empty_list(), list(int)) interning distinctly,
which is what makes most of the unbought rungs distinct at all); fz-kdt.107
is now UNMEASURABLE by the 13-fixture indistinguishable-arm gate (44 groups ->
0, count corrected from 45), NOT retired. Corrected in three places: the
ADDRESS_COLLAPSE_DEPTH cap applies inside is_pure_list_family ONLY; tuple, map
and resource recurse uncapped.

THIS DOES NOT UNBLOCK fz-kdt.120, verified independently twice: with this rule
applied AND the empty-list cleaner deleted, all seven fixtures still move and
List.reduce_cont/3[list(int), empty_list(), a2] still publishes {:done,
empty_list()} on a fully exact key. fz-kdt.210 owns that (a ground seed
instantiating a @spec return variable, met into the published return by
refine_call_return).

GATE: Coordinator gate on the folded commit, rebased onto fz-kdt.194 (marker COORD-GATE-1788464279): fmt clean, zero build warnings, clippy clean, doctests clean, lib 1709 passed / 0 failed / 5 ignored, fixture matrix single-threaded 509 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored.

comments.text: fz-kdt.183 landed (2e0bb2706): unblocked. Reproducer: step/2 with a {:done, acc} slot keyed TupleFields({0: Whole}) -- the key names the tag while the return IS acc. The forwarding rule does not touch it; it fires in the library only because Enum.reduce_finish/1 is non-recursive. (The source is in the 183 research artifacts as g0n.fz; reconstruct from this description.)

A SECOND, SHARPER REPRODUCER and a corpus consequence, from the fz-kdt.120 re-cut research (2026-09-03, ca23b676f). Your shape is what blocks fz-kdt.120. Enum.reduce/3 finishes through `reduce_finish({:done, a} | ..) :: a`. The first ascent rung's argument is `{:done, []}`, and because the tuple FIELD is freight (masked TupleFields({0: Whole}), keying the tag only) while the return IS that field, `a` binds `[]` and the join-only ladder never re-narrows -- Enum.reverse/1([int]) types as `[]`. Measured consequence: the fz-f98.16 empty-list cleaner in arrow_match.rs is the only thing discarding that stale binding today. Delete the cleaner (which fz-kdt.120 must do, and which fz-kdt.184 deliberately left inert for it) and SEVEN corpus fixtures produce WRONG ANSWERS -- 00276, 00277, 00420, enum_map_family, enum_take_drop_split, fz_f98_range_map_converges, mailbox_closure_enum_hofs -- with Enum.map/to_list/with_index collapsing to []. So this ticket is not only a precision matter: it is load-bearing for correctness the moment the masking cleaner goes. fz-kdt.120 is now marked BLOCKED BY this ticket. Red-first for you should include: with the acc field keyed, `Enum.reverse/1([int])` types as [int] and not [], and the seven fixtures stay correct with the cleaner deleted.

CORRECTION FROM MEASUREMENT -- my earlier comment on this ticket was wrong, and the coordinator withdraws it. I claimed this ticket was fz-kdt.120's blocker, inferring it from the shape of the {:done, acc} rung. The fz-kdt.199 research measured it stacked and REFUTED that: with this ticket's rule applied AND the empty-list cleaner deleted, all seven fixtures still move and Enum.reverse/1([int]) still types as []. The wrong return sits on List.reduce_cont/3[list(int), empty_list(), a2] -- a key with NOTHING collapsed -- so no keying rule can reach it. The real blocker is fz-kdt.210 (a ground seed instantiating a @spec return variable, which refine_call_return then meets into the published return). The `fz-kdt.199 blocks fz-kdt.120` dependency has been removed.

THIS TICKET STANDS ON ITS OWN, and is wider than its body says. Measured at ca23b676f: `walk({:go, acc}, n)` keys G.walk/2[{:go, list(a0_1_e)}, int] -- field 1 is the address var, the local mask is TupleFields({0: Whole}), and forwarded_inputs finds NO forward edge at all (both self-calls hand slot 0 a Tuple CONSTRUCTION, opaque under fz-kdt.183's rule). That one key publishes non_empty_list(binary) | non_empty_list(int), and a @spec strings([binary]) consumer turns it into error[spec/violation] ([binary] | [int]) -- a real wrong diagnostic on a legitimate program. AND: `loop(0, junk), do: junk` -- fz-kdt.183's OWN first keying law, blessed as "freight must key ONE activation" -- has the identical defect at base. So that law is a COST pin, not a correctness one, and this ticket is what makes it safe.

title: A returned tuple FIELD at a recursive key is freight: a {:done, acc} slot masked TupleFields({0: Whole}) keys only the tag while the return IS acc, so two users still share one joined return
